scope: ordinary uncompressed unicast Read CMD03, complete legal length/ATTR geometry; independent semantic model with local VC0/VC-credit profile
references: Common 2.0 Table2-2 pp49-52 and sections2.7.4.4-6/Table2-7 p55: fields, length and first/last DWORD enables
Common 2.0 section2.8 pp74-75: 256-byte boundary, natural lanes, ignored disabled bytes
Common 2.0 section2.7.5/Table2-15 pp62-64 and sections2.7.5.1-3/Table2-16 pp64-65: modes, status, LAST and DataError
Common 2.0 section2.7.8 pp71-72: complete response resources and ordered Multi-Beat transfer
Common 2.0 Table5-29/30 pp137-139: natural uncompressed fields

request.beat_count: number of distinct natural64-byte blocks touched by the DWORD interval, 1..4

byte_enables.attr_low_nibble: first DWORD byte enables, bit0 is its lowest address byte
byte_enables.attr_high_nibble: last DWORD enables when length>0; completely ignored for length0
byte_enables.zero_or_sparse_nibbles: legal; structural response Beat count does not shrink

request.raw_data_mapping: Beat j lane b corresponds to (address & ~63)+64*j+b; inactive lanes are not compacted
request.asi_metadata: unsigned2/8 opaque values preserved; no address-translation or coherence inference

response_events.type: ReadResponse is one reconstructed natural64-byte Beat event, not a packed TL Header/Data object
response_events.status_consistency: all Beats in one transaction use the same status
response_events.error_tenure: all original N Beats still required for every nonzero legal status
response_events.single: num_beats0; distinct OFFSET0..N-1 may arrive in any order; LAST only on final arriving Beat
response_events.multi: num_beatsN-1; exact OFFSET0..N-1 and final LAST, no same-port response interleaving inside the burst
response_events.multi_header_decode: decode_response_burst requires exactly LEN+1 full Data Beats, reconstructs event OFFSET/LAST, ignores invalid raw OFFSET and unresolved raw Header LAST reduction
response_events.multi_header_last_caveat: the decoder policy is an explicit interpretation pending Table5-30 clarification, not an invented normative bit restriction
response_events.send_policy: encode_response and memory_read deliberately emit Single-Beat mode
response_events.identity: (port,tag), destination must equal local ID; source is debug-only
response_events.poison: independent boolean per event, never inferred from status; completion retains a relative Beat poison bitmap

collector: reserve(request): retain complete request identity/geometry and response capacity
receive(response): atomic validation/save; returns Completion only after all N Beats
peek(port,tag): immutable Completion or None; stable under application backpressure
retire(port,tag): release identity only after complete application acceptance
reset(): clear owned Tags and multi-burst ownership
occupancy: includes completed but not yet application-retired Tags

local_memory_and_application_policy: ByteMemory owns immutable bytes and a full57-bit base; memory_read is one backend-result event and increments executions exactly once even for zero-BE/errors.
The declared DWORD interval must lie in the memory window regardless of BE; out-of-window status0 requests yield status3. Explicit nonzero status takes priority.
Raw success Beat lanes preserve memory bytes wherever mapped; natural Beat padding outside the memory window is zero. No requested-byte compaction occurs.
Nonzero backend statuses return N full manufactured Data Beats. error_pattern defaults0 and also permits0xff; the receiver does not require one pattern.
Successful unpoisoned Completion.data is relative naturally aligned data with inactive bytes zero. requested_mask always records geometry; valid_mask equals requested_mask only for safe success.

Any error or poison suppresses all application data and valid_mask while retaining status, N, requested_mask and poison bitmap. Whole-transaction poison suppression is a conservative local API policy.
Invalid response events raise local exceptions without mutating saved identity, status, mode, Beat data or ownership. Exceptions are not wire error statuses.

known_vectors.method: fixed request and response literals from independent binary-field worksheets, not model-generated expected values

verification.oracle: enumerated natural byte positions for first/last DWORD and middle bytes, independent of model nibble arithmetic
mutations: natural lanes compressed to request address

limitations: Semantic events are not cycle-accurate UPLI handshakes, TL credit/framing, DL replay or a proof of RTL execution.
This collector owns Read Tags only; shared Read/Write allocation remains a separate integration responsibility.
No compressed/cache, security, multicast, INC, atomic or vendor-command handling is inferred.
Reset clears state but cannot identify a stale wire response after legal same-Tag reuse without an external epoch scheme.
No memory-coherence, ordering barrier, timer/watchdog or recovery protocol is supplied by this model.
Model/RTL agreement does not constitute independent consortium compliance or physical signoff.
